title: Axial gauge on the periodic lattice: every gauge field reduces to Polyakov loops on one slice
claim: For any group G, any d, L ≥ 1, any direction τ and any link configuration U on the periodic lattice (ℤ/Lℤ)^d, the Lean theorem Contribution.result constructs an explicit gauge transformation g (parallel transport along the τ-line from the slice x_τ = 0) such that: (1) every τ-link off the last slice becomes trivial, (gU)_{x,τ} = 1 whenever x_τ + 1 < L; (2) on the last slice, x_τ = L − 1, the remaining τ-link equals the Polyakov loop P(b) = U_{b,τ} U_{b+τ,τ} ⋯ U_{b+(L−1)τ,τ} of the τ-line through x, with b its point on the slice x_τ = 0; (3) every class-function plaquette action, including the Wilson action of accepted contribution pr-10, is unchanged. This is the axial (temporal) gauge used to build the transfer matrix and Hamiltonian formulation and in Faddeev–Popov arguments on finite lattices. On the torus the τ-links cannot all be removed. The statement pins down the exact obstruction: one Polyakov loop per τ-line. It is the gauge-invariant data that center symmetry acts on.
novelty: This builds on the accepted track result pr-10 (lattice, plaquettes, gauge action, class-function action invariance), which it imports and uses. The mathematics is classical (axial/temporal gauge, e.g. Creutz's and Montvay–Münster's textbooks). In the external Lean library lgt (Douglas), the corresponding step is not proved. lgt's GaugeFixing.lean states that constructing the gauge transform that fixes the axial links 'requires' the tree argument, and its faddeevPopov theorem takes the Faddeev–Popov identity as a hypothesis, hFP. This bundle supplies an explicit, axiom-clean construction for the periodic lattice, any group and any direction, together with the exact Polyakov-loop residue on the last slice.

attribution.contributions: The Lean construction, statements and proofs were written by an AI coding agent (Claude, Anthropic) on behalf of the wallet holder, who directed the submission. No third-party code is included.

limitations: This is a purely classical, configuration-level statement. It does not prove the Faddeev–Popov identity for the Haar/Wilson measure (Fubini and Haar invariance are not formalized), and it does not construct the transfer matrix. Only τ-links are fixed. Gauge fixing of spatial links (a full maximal-tree gauge) and the residual τ-independent gauge freedom are not treated. Uniqueness of the gauge-fixed form is not proved. Nothing here addresses the quantum theory, the continuum limit or the mass gap.
